summary: C-0005: The strict 'trance required' (qualitative state) hypothesis is largely RULED OUT, but the broader 'is there a real altered state' question remains open and is best framed as a continuum, not a dichotomy
content: CLAIM C-0005: Oakley & Halligan (2013) concluded neuroimaging data converge in 'ruling out the qualitative state hypothesis' — the view that suggested perceptual alterations CANNOT occur unless the subject is in a hypnotic trance. This is reinforced by Dienes et al.'s preregistered Stroop equivalence (suggestion ≈ volitional request) and by the repeated finding that induction adds little for many participants. So the STRONG/TRADITIONAL state claim is rejected. BUT this does not entail pure non-state: measurable brain changes DO occur (C-0001), and the absence of a unique fingerprint is an absence-of-evidence problem. The field now treats this as fuzzy points on a continuum (Oakley & Halligan) rather than a binary. SUPPORTS: both strict-state and pure-compliance extremes are disconfirmed; the live question is the nature/degree of the altered processing.
